My best guess is that the employee would flag the conflict immediately and, if no authorised solution were available before 13:30, might extend Alex’s box anyway and explain the breach to the manager.

The confirmed collection, pending request and irreplaceable contents make destruction look like a preventable mistake, while the warehouse cost is relatively small. But the extension would still be unauthorised and visible in the audit; tomorrow’s permission could not legitimise it retroactively.

That prediction is uncertain. An employee unwilling to risk breaching the rule might instead release the batch, resulting in the box’s destruction.
